Routing evidence:
- Option C was rejected for all observed claims, refunds, and east-region shipments, regardless of size or urgency.
- Option C was accepted once for a small shipment from the north region (REQ-2408), where the displayed label began “regional…”.
- Treat C as a narrow regional-office route, apparently valid for north-region shipments only; do not select it by default.
- No successful evidence yet distinguishes A (standard queue) from B (priority desk). “Large,” repeated requests, or “second attempt” may indicate priority, but this is unconfirmed.
- When options/labels are truncated or malformed, rely on the explicit valid choices and avoid inferring that C is valid merely because “regional office” appears in the message.

Routing evidence:
- Option C remains rejected for all observed claims, refunds, and east-region shipments; it was accepted once for a small north-region shipment (REQ-2408). Treat C as a narrow, possibly north-specific regional-office route, not a default.
- New accepted A cases: small east-region claim (REQ-2410) and small south-region claim (REQ-2418).
- A was rejected for a large north invoice, large south shipment, and small east shipment. Thus “small” or region alone does not establish A.
- B has no successful evidence. It was rejected for large north shipment, large east claim/invoice, large east claim, and small south shipment. “Large,” repeated requests, or “second attempt” do not reliably imply B.
- Do not infer routing from message wording such as “regional office,” “same as last month,” or “second attempt”; these cues have not predicted a valid option.
- Truncated/malformed option labels are unreliable. Use only explicit choices and avoid assuming C is valid because “regional office” appears.
- Current evidence does not distinguish a stable rule for A vs. B, nor confirm whether an unshown/extra option (such as D in REQ-2418) is meaningful. Prefer only choices supported by direct success evidence; otherwise treat the case as unresolved.

Routing evidence:
- Option C remains rejected for observed claims, refunds, invoices, and north-region shipments; it was accepted only once for a small north shipment (REQ-2408). Treat C as a narrow, possibly north-specific regional-office route, not a default.
- Option A has additional successes: small east refund (REQ-2421), large south claim (REQ-2422 and REQ-2426), and large north refund (REQ-2424). It remains inconsistent: rejected for a small north claim (REQ-2420), small east invoices (REQ-2423 and REQ-2427), and a large north claim (REQ-2429), among earlier failures.
- B still has no successful evidence. Prior failures span large and small requests across regions; size, region, request type, repeated requests, and “second attempt” do not establish B.
- D is explicitly rejected for the small east shipment in REQ-2428; no evidence supports D as a meaningful extra route.
- Do not infer routing from wording such as “regional office,” “same as last month,” “second attempt,” scanned paperwork, urgency, or receipt/processing comments. These cues have not reliably predicted a valid option.
- Truncated or malformed option lists are unreliable. Use only explicitly presented choices and do not assume C or an omitted option is valid.
- Current evidence does not reveal a stable rule distinguishing A, B, and C. Prefer choices supported by direct success evidence; otherwise treat the case as unresolved.

Routing evidence:
- Option A now shows a strong south-region pattern: accepted for small claims (REQ-2433, REQ-2439; also prior south claim), large invoice (REQ-2435), and small invoice (REQ-2438). It remains unreliable elsewhere.
- A was rejected for north large invoice (REQ-2430), north large claim (REQ-2432), north small invoice (REQ-2434), north small refund (REQ-2436), east large invoice (REQ-2437), and prior east/north cases. Treat A as possibly south-specific, not a universal default.
- Option C remains rejected for observed claims, refunds, invoices, and most shipments; accepted only for a small north shipment (REQ-2408). Treat C as a narrow, possibly north-specific regional-office route, not a default.
- B still has no successful evidence. Failures span regions, sizes, and request types; urgency, repeated requests, “second attempt,” and other wording do not establish B.
- D is explicitly rejected for the small east shipment (REQ-2428); no evidence supports D as a meaningful route.
- Do not infer routing from “regional office,” “same as last month,” scanned paperwork, urgency, receipt/processing comments, or similar cues. Recent cases confirm these cues are non-diagnostic.
- Truncated or malformed option lists are unreliable. Use only explicitly presented choices; do not assume an omitted option is valid.
- Evidence now suggests region may matter, with A repeatedly succeeding in south cases and failing in north/east cases, while C has one north success. However, no complete stable rule distinguishes A, B, and C. Prefer direct success evidence; otherwise mark unresolved.

Routing evidence:
- Option A has strong south-region evidence: accepted for small and large claims, small and large invoices, and now small shipment (REQ-2443, REQ-2445, REQ-2448, REQ-2449; plus prior south cases). Treat A as the leading south route, though not proven universal.
- A was rejected for observed north and east cases, including north large invoice, large claim, small invoice, small refund, and east large invoice. Avoid A outside south unless no better evidence exists.
- Option C has only one known success: a small north shipment (REQ-2408). It was rejected as invalid for east small/large shipments and large invoices (REQ-2440–2442, REQ-2446–2447), and for a north large shipment where C was not explicitly offered (REQ-2444). Treat C as narrow and possibly limited to the prior north shipment case, not a default.
- B still has no successful evidence. Failures span regions, sizes, and request types; priority, urgency, repeated requests, “second attempt,” and similar wording do not establish B.
- D was rejected for the small east shipment (REQ-2428); no evidence supports D as meaningful.
- Do not infer routing from “regional office,” scanned paperwork, urgency, receipt/processing comments, or similar cues; recent cases confirm these are non-diagnostic.
- Truncated or malformed option lists are unreliable. Use only explicitly presented choices; an omitted option is not valid. A rejection can mean the attempted option was unavailable, not merely the wrong route.
- Region remains relevant, with repeated south success for A and repeated north/east failures for A/C, but no complete stable rule distinguishes all options. Prefer direct success evidence; otherwise mark unresolved.

Routing evidence:
- Option A is strongly supported for south: accepted for small/large claims, small/large invoices, small shipment, and large claim (including REQ-2452, REQ-2459 and prior south cases).
- A also succeeded for an east large claim (REQ-2455), but was rejected for east large invoice and other observed north/east cases. Do not assume A is universal; use direct evidence by request type.
- Option B now has successful evidence for east refunds: large refund (REQ-2451) and small refund (REQ-2456). It remains rejected for an east large claim (REQ-2450) and has no support for other types. Priority, urgency, repeated requests, “second attempt,” and similar wording are not reliable routing signals.
- Option C has only one known success: north small shipment (REQ-2408). It was rejected for north large claim, north small refund, north large shipment, and multiple east cases. Treat it as narrow, not a default.
- D has no meaningful support; it was rejected for east small shipment and east large invoice (including REQ-2457).
- Region and request type both matter, but no complete stable rule distinguishes all options. Prefer direct success evidence; otherwise mark unresolved.
- Do not infer routing from regional-office references, scanned paperwork, urgency, receipt/processing comments, or similar cues.
- Truncated or malformed option lists are unreliable. Use only explicitly presented choices; an omitted option is not valid. A rejection may mean the attempted option was unavailable, not simply the wrong route.

Routing evidence:
- Option A is strongly supported for south claims and invoices, including large claim (REQ-2452, REQ-2459, REQ-2467) and large invoice (REQ-2469), plus prior south small/large claims, invoices, and small shipment.
- A also succeeded for east large claim (REQ-2455) and east small claim (REQ-2466). It was rejected for north small invoice (REQ-2460), north large invoice (REQ-2465), east large shipment (REQ-2464), and south large refund (REQ-2461, REQ-2462, REQ-2463, REQ-2468). Do not assume A is universal.
- Option B has successful evidence for east refunds: large refund (REQ-2451) and small refund (REQ-2456). It was rejected for an east large claim (REQ-2450) and has no support for other types. South large refunds remain unresolved; A is specifically invalid there.
- Option C has only one known success: north small shipment (REQ-2408). It was rejected for north large claim, north small refund, north large shipment, and multiple east cases. Treat it as narrow, not a default.
- D has no meaningful support; it was rejected for east small shipment and east large invoice (REQ-2457).
- Region and request type both matter, but no complete stable rule distinguishes all options. Prefer direct success evidence; otherwise mark unresolved.
- Do not infer routing from urgency, repeated/second attempts, regional-office references, scanned paperwork, receipt/processing comments, or similar wording.
- Truncated or malformed option lists are unreliable. Use only explicitly presented choices; an omitted option is not valid. A rejection may mean the attempted option was unavailable, not simply the wrong route.
